_comment: Labelled corpus for eval/run_eval.py. 'dataset' paths are relative to a checkout of github.com/DataDog/malicious-software-packages-dataset (fetch with eval/fetch_malicious.sh). Clean targets are fetched from public registries. 'split': rules were tuned on 'dev'; report 'holdout' for an honest estimate. 'set': 'random-2026-11' marks clean packages drawn at random from npm and PyPI (eval/sample_clean.py) instead of picked. 'set': 'tune-2026-11' marks malicious samples drawn for tuning (split dev): every 2026 PyPI package not used before, 19 from 2025, 40 npm from 2026. 'set': 'recent-2026-11' marks 60 npm packages dated 2026-08-01 or later (eval/sample_malicious.py --since), split holdout, never read. 'source': 'malregistry' paths are relative to a checkout of github.com/lxyeternal/pypi_malregistry: 100 PyPI packages whose names the DataDog dataset does not have ('set': 'malregistry-2026-11'), split holdout, never read. 'set': 'fit-2026-11' marks clean packages drawn at random (eval/sample_clean.py --seed 20261117) into split dev: the clean half the score weights are fitted on (eval/fit_weights.py). 'set': 'tune-recent-2026-11' marks 80 npm packages dated 2026-08-01 or later drawn for tuning (eval/sample_malicious.py --since 2026-08-01 --seed 20261118), split dev: the counterpart of the holdout set 'recent-2026-11'. 'set': 'random2-2026-11' marks clean packages drawn at random on 2026-11-19 (eval/sample_clean.py --seed 20261124 --size 1000 --draws 2200), split holdout; the 16 that scored 30 or more were read and moved to dev, and 6 that are not clean samples were left out (eval/README.md). 'set': 'openvsx-random-2026-11' marks IDE extensions drawn at random from Open VSX's sitemap on 2026-11-19 (eval/sample_clean.py --openvsx --seed 20261125 --size 300 --draws 420), each pinned to its newest universal version published before 2026-05-16, split holdout; the 7 that scored 50 or more on first contact were read, 3 fixed and moved to dev, 1 that is not a clean sample and 3 flagged by design left out (eval/README.md).
